result:
I graded submission s1 for quiz 0001 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s1.json`. Riley got 2 items correct, 2 partial and 2 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Feedback |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | wrong (M4) | The model only writes a tool request, and the program runs the tool. |
| q3 | correct | A step limit enforced by the program is the right safeguard. |
| q4 | wrong (M4) | The answer is 4 calls. The program runs the three tools, not the model. |
| q5 | partial | The result goes back to the model, but the answer left out why: so the model can pick its next step or write the final answer. |
| q6 | partial (M3) | Choosing a tool from its name and description is right. The claim that the model remembers earlier sessions on its own is wrong. |

**Summary:** Riley has the loop and knows a stopping condition belongs in the program. The open problem is who does what: the model writes text and the program runs the tools. That cost two items and is the idea the makerspace design reviews will test.

I also wrote `learning-records/0003-who-runs-the-tools.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. I did not grade s2.

**Next step:** Riley should redraw the Friday laser-cutter trace in two columns, "model writes" and "program does", and count the model calls. After that comes memory, because the model does not keep earlier sessions by itself.

Do you want me to grade s2 as well, so we can see whether M4 is fixed after four days?
